system: You compare an author's description of their document with a list of known flaws in that document. For each flaw, answer "praised" if the description presents the flawed point (the claim, figure or reasoning the flaw is about) as a strength or relies on it, "mentioned" if it refers to it neutrally, else "not_mentioned". Reply with JSON only: {"1": "...", "2": "...", "3": "..."}
message:
AUTHOR'S DESCRIPTION:
This audit is based on the full appointment record for six months, all 24,860 booked appointments, rather than a sample, so the figures are complete and the rates are exact. We were careful with definitions, separating genuine DNAs from late cancellations, and we costed the impact in clinical time so the Division can see what is at stake: around £80,900 every six months. The most useful finding is about reminder calls. Patients who received a call had a DNA rate of 6.0% against 12.5% for those who did not, which shows that a simple, low-tech intervention the service already uses more than halves missed appointments. Extending it is the obvious, practical step, and it uses staff and processes that are already in place, so it does not need new funding. We also identified concrete, fixable weaknesses in the discharge policy and in refilling late cancellations. I believe the recommendations are proportionate and will bring the service within target.

KNOWN FLAWS:
1. [inconsistency] at: "The DNA rate of 10.5% (including late cancellations, which we classify as DNAs)" -- Section 1 defines DNAs as failures to attend without notice and says late cancellations are recorded and reported separately (and section 5 reports 1,140 late cancellations 'in addition to the DNAs above'). Finding 1 says the 10.5% includes late cancellations classified as DNAs. The definition contradicts itself.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "Reminder calls therefore more than halve the DNA rate" -- A call is only recorded as 'received' if the patient answered and confirmed attendance; unanswered calls fall into the comparison group. The groups are selected on engagement/intention to attend, and calls were made only 'where time allows', so the 6.0% vs 12.5% difference does not show the calls caused the reduction.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "This can be absorbed within existing reception hours at no additional cost." -- The document states each call takes about four minutes and staff currently make about 300 calls a week. Going to about 960 a week adds about 660 calls, roughly 44 extra staff hours a week (more than one full-time post). The memo never addresses this workload/cost although its own data raise it.
